description: The hand-verified expected result for the positive Checkov fixture, which is harness/artifacts/raw/checkov.json byte for byte. Every value was derived by reading the fixture and the authored contracts in harness/lib/normalize/, never by running the adapter and recording what it printed. Where this file and harness/lib/normalize/adapters/checkov.py disagree, the disagreement is the finding: diagnose it rather than overwriting this file to match.
scanner_class_note: Fixed for this tool by AAP 0.5.4's class table and carried unchanged on every row. It does not vary with check_type, with the reporting framework or with record content; trivy is the single tool whose class is decided per record, from the section the record was read from.

fixture.top_level_form_note: A single report object, which is the form a Checkov artifact takes when one framework reports -- here the dockerfile framework over the three Kubernetes Dockerfiles. The shape varies with the artifact's content rather than with the invocation, so the multi-framework array form of these same records is covered by oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/checkov-alt-shape.json and must produce these same rows.
fixture.results_buckets_note: The artifact's results object carries results.failed_checks and nothing else -- no passed_checks, no skipped_checks and no parsing_errors key at all, because the runner invokes checkov with --compact. That absence is preserved rather than filled in, which is what makes this fixture the artifact: an absent bucket must be read as zero, and the counters below assert it is.
fixture.summary_note: The report's own summary object, quoted as the artifact carries it. It is the tool's statement about itself and is never used as the record count: the count unit below is the one normalize.reconcile.count_records walks independently of row construction. Its passed value of 201 is a case in point -- the artifact's results object carries no passed_checks bucket, so the 201 passes it reports are visible only in this summary and reach no counter and no row.
fixture.provenance: captured -- the whole raw artifact, unmodified
fixture.provenance_note: AAP 0.6.2 defines a positive fixture as an unmodified captured excerpt of the tool's own output, with the enclosing structure preserved. This artifact is 8,380 bytes, so no excerpting was needed and the fixture is the whole file: check_type, the results object with its single bucket, all six failed checks and the tool's own summary, byte for byte. Its sha256 therefore equals the raw artifact's, which is the strongest provenance available -- not a selection asserted to be faithful, but the same bytes.
fixture.provenance_assertion: Asserted, not described: test_checkov_adapter.py's RawArtifactProvenanceTests opens harness/artifacts/raw/checkov.json and requires this fixture's byte size and sha256 to equal the artifact's, every failed check to be identical under canonical comparison, check_type, the exact set of buckets present in results and the summary object to match, and the fixture to introduce no member the artifact lacks. The raw artifact's absence is an explicit failure naming the path rather than a skip.

feature_cases_live_in_a_derived_fixture.why: The artifact carries no passed_checks, no skipped_checks and no parsing_errors, so the failures-only contract and the parsing-errors-as-status-evidence contract cannot be asserted non-vacuously against it. Those cases are not deleted: they are exercised against an explicitly derived fixture whose expected file declares it derived, states what it was derived from and names the cases it exists for. Authoring the buckets into this file instead would have meant claiming unmodified captured output for a document that was part invention, which is the claim AAP 0.6.2 does not permit to be approximate.

field_order_authority: harness/lib/normalize/emit.py, the FIELDS constant, of which harness/lib/normalize/adapters/checkov.py carries the authored copy AAP 0.6.4's import restriction requires. Every row below carries all twelve keys in that order, present-with-null rather than omitted.
absence_convention: Absence is JSON null here and in findings.json, and an empty field in findings.csv. tool, scanner_class, rule_id, message, severity_norm, path and in_scope are never absent -- a record whose path cannot be resolved is rejected and counted rather than emitted with a null path.

allowlist.note: in_scope is decided by that file alone. The globs are not copied here: the allowlist is the single authority and stays byte-exact. The glob each row matched is recorded per row under row_derivations. That the runner also reads the allowlist to build its 18 -d target roots is a fact about its reach, not about this field.

resolution_context.worked_example: AAP 0.5.3's first user example, carried in unchanged. Checkov's file_path is relative to the scan target and carries a leading slash, alongside file_abs_path holding the filesystem-absolute path and repo_file_path a root-relative path that also carries a leading slash. The expected path is the leading slash stripped and the remainder treated as root-relative, reconciled against the absolute file_abs_path the same record carries.
resolution_context.path_base_source: harness/artifacts/logs/runner-metadata.json, the checkov entry's path_base -- read as input, never assumed
resolution_context.runner_invocation: one checkov invocation carrying 18 root-relative -d target roots, recorded at runner-metadata.json tools.checkov.invocation_form. This is the fact that makes file_path ambiguous on its own.
resolution_context.anchor_rule: repo_file_path is root-relative and carries a leading slash, so exactly one slash is stripped and the remainder is the row's path. file_abs_path is filesystem-absolute and is relativized to the scan root. Both anchors are present on all six records here and resolve to the same string, so no disagreement is recorded and the anchor order never has to break a tie.
resolution_context.file_path_role: corroboration only. Under per_target_directory the slash-stripped file_path is relative to whichever -d root matched, so it corroborates by being a suffix of the anchored path -- and it is, on all six records. A disagreement would be recorded rather than resolved, and would never suppress the row.
resolution_context.why_file_path_alone_is_wrong: Stripping the slash off file_path and joining the remainder to the tree root names dockerfiles/spark/Dockerfile, a directory that does not exist at the root, and no row would then match the allowlist. Reading the same value as filesystem-absolute is the failure the worked example warns about: it relativizes to a long ../ chain and the row silently takes in_scope false, with nothing crashing. No expected path in this file begins with / or contains a ../ segment, and every row is in scope.
resolution_context.scan_root_source: harness/artifacts/logs/runner-metadata.json, spark_src and the checkov entry's resolved_scan_root
resolution_context.root_independence: Every row below holds for whatever absolute scan root the adapter is given: the path comes from repo_file_path, which is already root-relative and needs no root to resolve. No row carries an absolute path in any field. The absolute values that do appear in this file are quoted evidence rather than emitted data -- the recorded scan root, each record's own file_abs_path under row_derivations.path_cross_check, and the parsing-error entry Checkov reported verbatim -- and none of them reaches a row. One counter is root-dependent and is called out under counters_root_note.
resolution_context.severity_source: the record's own severity field, which is null on every failed check because severities require a licence and BC_API_KEY is deliberately absent. severity.resolve then states the absence rather than assuming a level: severity_native null, severity_norm Info, basis no_vocabulary. No CVSS score is consulted -- a misconfiguration carries none, and AAP 0.5.4's checkov row names severity and nothing else.
resolution_context.start_line_source: file_line_range[0], as an integer. An absent range or an explicitly null first element would yield null with no rejection, since absence is permitted for that field; a range that is present but not an array, and one that is an array carrying no first element, would each be malformed_record, and an unusable first element non_integer_start_line.
resolution_context.cwe_and_cve_source: the closed field set guideline, description, short_description, bc_category, benchmarks, details, vulnerability_details. Every one of them is null or an empty array on every record here, so no CWE or CVE token exists to collect and both fields are null on every row. check_name is deliberately outside that set: it is the row's message, and harvesting an identifier out of a message would put a weakness reference in the dataset that the record never made as a reference.
resolution_context.package_coordinate: null on every row. A misconfiguration names a location in a configuration file rather than a package, so no coordinate can be formed -- and that absence is not a rejection: AAP 0.5.4 attaches unformable_package_coordinate to a dependency-oriented record, which this is not.

failures_only.count_unit: one element of results.failed_checks[], the union across every report object in either top-level shape
failures_only.absent_bucket_rule: The runner invokes checkov with --compact, so the artifact's results object carries failed_checks alone. An absent bucket is read as zero: it contributes no record, no row and no rejection, and it is not a container fault -- results is an object and failed_checks is an array, so all three container-shape counters stay 0. That is what these zeros assert, and it is a different statement from 'the bucket was present and was excluded'.
failures_only.vacuity_note: Asserting failures-only over this artifact would be vacuous, and this file does not pretend otherwise: with nothing to exclude, an adapter that read every bucket would satisfy the row count here. The non-vacuous assertion lives on oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/derived-checkov-features.json, which carries three real passed checks, one skipped check whose identifier also appears on two emitted failures, and one parsing error -- and requires 5 rows from 5 failed checks. Naming that here is what keeps the two claims separate: this fixture proves the mapping of captured records, that one proves the exclusion.
failures_only.where_the_exclusion_is_asserted: oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/expected/derived-checkov-features.rows.json, and in test_checkov_adapter.py's FailuresOnlyTests and ParsingErrorsTests, which read that fixture for every bucket-dependent assertion.

counts.raw_count_unit: one element of results.failed_checks[] -- the unit normalize.reconcile.count_records walks independently of row construction
counts.row_count_note: 6 equals len(results.failed_checks) exactly, and it equals the artifact summary's own failed value of 6 -- which is corroboration rather than the source, since the summary is the tool's statement about itself and is never used as the count unit. Every record becomes a row and none is rejected, so rejections is 0 and the identity holds at 6 = 6 + 0.

counters_authority: harness/lib/normalize/adapters/checkov.py, COUNTER_KEYS as returned by new_counters(): nineteen authored keys, one path_kind_* per member of normalize.paths.PATH_KINDS and one severity_basis_* per member of normalize.severity.BASIS_VALUES -- twenty-eight in all, every one an int.
counters_note: The four counters AAP 0.5.4 has reported per tool -- multi_location_records, multi_valued_cwe_records, multi_valued_cve_records and non_filesystem_paths -- are all 0 here and all four are keys of this adapter's own set, so each is a measured 0 rather than an absence. passed_checks_observed, skipped_checks_observed and parsing_errors are 0 because the artifact's results object carries none of those three buckets: an absent bucket contributes 0 and is not a container fault, which is why reports_without_results_object and reports_without_failed_checks_array are also 0. The non-zero values of those three counters are asserted over oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/derived-checkov-features.json, so a zero here never stands in for the exclusion contract. rows_in_scope plus rows_out_of_scope is 6 + 0 = 6, one measurement split rather than a second count of the same thing.
counters_root_note: path_corroboration_recorded is the one value here that depends on which root the adapter is given. Under the recorded scan root /opt/spark-src the two anchors resolve to the same string and file_path is a suffix of it, so nothing is recorded and the counter is 0. Given some other absolute root, file_abs_path would relativize to a ../ chain, disagree with repo_file_path, and be recorded on all five rows -- the counter would be 5 while every row below stayed byte-identical, because the path comes from the anchor the disagreement does not move.

alt_shape_invariant.rows_must_equal: exactly the six rows below, in this order, field for field
alt_shape_invariant.why: That fixture is a two-element array -- a kubernetes report whose failed_checks array is empty, and a dockerfile report whose failed_checks are this fixture's six records as whole unedited objects in the same order. The union of results.failed_checks[] across its report objects is therefore the same six records in the same order, and the two shapes reduce to one sequence of report objects before any record is read, so identical content in either form must produce identical rows. That equality is what the dual-shape assertion tests, and it could not be asserted of two forks of the record loop.
alt_shape_invariant.shape_only_transformation: The array form is a shape transformation of this fixture and nothing else: the six failed-check objects, this fixture's check_type and this fixture's summary are carried across unedited, and the only material added is one empty framework report, which contributes no record. test_checkov_adapter.py asserts that directly -- it extracts the ordered whole failed_checks objects from both committed fixtures and compares them element for element, before any adapter is invoked, so an edit to a field the adapter ignores cannot pass unnoticed.
alt_shape_invariant.counters_that_differ: Only the shape-dependent ones: top_level_form_array 1 and top_level_form_object 0 there against the reverse here, and reports 2 there against 1 here. Every other counter above is unchanged, because the records are the same records.

scope_of_this_file.records_only_this_tool: These are checkov's rows and nothing else. Another tool reporting a finding at the same location produces its own rows in its own expected file; no comparison, no deduplication and no ranking is made here, and nothing in these rows characterises a finding as real, important or a false positive.
scope_of_this_file.no_secret_value: No field carries a secret or any content from check_result.results_configuration. message is check_name and nothing else -- never assembled from check_id, bc_check_id, guideline, resource or code_block -- so the command text and shell content those records quote reach no row. This tree is committed to git.
scope_of_this_file.no_inference: A record whose path could not be established with certainty would be a counted rejection, never a path picked from two candidates. That case is covered by oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/reject-checkov-unresolvable-path.json, not by any row here.
scope_of_this_file.no_dedup: Three rows carry rule_id CKV_DOCKER_9 and three carry CKV_DOCKER_2, and each of the three Dockerfiles contributes two rows. All six are emitted. Nothing here collapses repeated rule identifiers or repeated paths, and no row is characterised as a duplicate of another (AAP 0.3.2).

corroboration.note: The committed dataset carries exactly six checkov rows -- the artifact's six failed checks, which is what this fixture is -- and all twelve fields of all six agree with the rows below, in this order. Corroboration recorded after the fact, not the source of these values: each was derived from the fixture and the authored contracts, so a future disagreement between this file and the adapter is a finding to diagnose rather than a diff to apply.
corroboration.every_record_has_a_dataset_counterpart: True of this fixture and of no derived one: the fixture is the artifact, so its record set and the dataset's checkov rows are the same six records. That is what makes the corroboration above total rather than partial.
corroboration.pin_evidence: The three files these rows name were read at the pinned commit 59b8a4489c878fa3a9aa6b7fbae760f2fc80eb9d: dockerfiles/spark/Dockerfile is 71 lines, bindings/python/Dockerfile 46 and bindings/R/Dockerfile 47, so no start_line or range bound below exceeds its own file.
